events.text: Your people come to the temples with the same dream: a grey bird circling over the world you made, lower every night. The priests ask you what it means. You know what it means.

choices.text: Tell the priests to bring the harvest in early

effects.log: The harvest comes in early. Whatever is coming will find less to take.

choices.text: Walk the world's high places and look

effects.log: From the highest mountain you can see it, a stain at the edge of the sky. Next year.

choices.text: Say nothing yet

effects.log: You say nothing. The bird keeps circling in their dreams.

events.text: The world you made has gone very quiet. Its rivers run slow, its birds have flown south in the wrong season, and every old person in it says the same thing: something is coming down on us.

choices.text: Count what your world has to lose

effects.log: You count. It has a great deal to lose. That is why it is coming.

choices.text: Promise your people you will stand over them

effects.log: The promise goes from temple to temple faster than any messenger. Now you have to keep it.

choices.text: Send the priests to calm them

effects.log: The priests calm them, mostly. You do not feel calm at all.

events.text: Heaven tests what is precious. In the world you made the sky has turned the colour of an old bruise from edge to edge, and the people have stopped working to watch it.

choices.text: Go down and stand among them

effects.log: They see you standing in the market square and go back to work. Faith is a strange thing to carry.

choices.text: Study the colour of the sky

effects.log: You learn the shape of the blow before it falls. It is a large shape.

choices.text: Look for the weakest place in the world's defence

effects.log: You find it. A river valley, full of farms. You will remember where it is.

events.text: The incense in your domain's temples burns sideways this morning, all of it, towards the east. Your priests come to you with very careful faces.

choices.text: Ask them what the old records say

effects.log: The old records say this happened once before, and the god who held the domain was not ready.

choices.text: Tell them to keep the temples open

effects.log: The temples stay open. The worshippers keep coming, and look east.

choices.text: Go and look east yourself

effects.log: East of your domain the light is wrong. Next year, then.

events.text: Every god's domain is a thing heaven gave and can test. Yours is about to be tested hard: the stars over it have rearranged themselves into a shape the old gods recognise and do not like.

choices.text: Ask an older god what is coming

effects.log: The older god looks at the stars for a long time and says only: be there.

choices.text: Look at what you hold, and what it is worth

effects.log: It is worth a great deal. Heaven has noticed that too.

choices.text: Tell your worshippers to pray harder

effects.log: They pray harder. The stars do not move.

events.text: Your disciples have started finding cracks in the isle's foundation stones, fine as hairs, every morning a few more. The oldest of them says the cloud-sea below is restless.

choices.text: Walk the cracks with the disciples

effects.log: You walk them all, every crack, and the disciples walk behind you a little less afraid.

choices.text: Tell the disciples to start laying arrays

effects.log: They start that afternoon. Arrays are never wasted.

choices.text: Say the isle has stood worse

effects.log: It has. Whether it will stand this, you do not say.

events.text: In the night the whole isle you built drops a hand's width in the cloud-sea, and every bell on it rings at once. By morning everyone knows: a great calamity is gathering, and it is gathering here.

choices.text: Gather the sect in the great hall

effects.log: You tell them the truth. Nobody leaves. You did not expect to be moved by that, and you are.

choices.text: Go down under the isle and look

effects.log: Under the isle the clouds are the colour of iron. It is coming.

choices.text: Begin counting what can be carried away

effects.log: You count. It is less than you hoped. Better to stand, then.

events.text: The first sign is the birds: every bird on the Isles in the air at once, flying away from the same horizon. Then the sound comes, low and endless, of a great many things running.

choices.text: Go up to the highest place and look

effects.log: You see it from far off: a tide of fallen beasts, more than you can count, coming this way.

choices.text: Check your weapons

effects.log: Your weapons are ready. You find you are, too.

choices.text: Find out who is already standing on the line

effects.log: Fewer than you hoped. More than you feared.

events.text: Once in a few lifetimes the wild places above the clouds empty themselves all at once. Old immortals say it is the beasts remembering what they were. Today the wild places are emptying.

choices.text: Listen to the old immortals' stories of the last one

effects.log: In the last one, a famous immortal stood alone on a bridge for three days. Nobody remembers who ran.

choices.text: Think about what a tide leaves behind

effects.log: Cores, hides, bones grown in qi for ten thousand years. A tide is a disaster and a harvest.

choices.text: Think about who will need help

effects.log: You think of three places at once. You cannot be at all three.

variants: The wild places above the clouds are emptying all at once, as they do once in a few lifetimes. The old immortals say the beasts are remembering what they were. Today they remember.

events.text: The gods do not speak of fear, but they move their thrones further from the edge of the Divine Realm this morning. A herd of divine beasts has broken its old bonds, and it is running.

choices.text: Watch the herd from a high place

effects.log: Even running wild, they are beautiful. That will not make them gentler.

choices.text: Ask which pantheon is going to stop it

effects.log: Each pantheon is waiting for another one to go first. Of course they are.

choices.text: Go and find where it will strike first

effects.log: You find it. A valley of temples, full of worshippers who have not been told.

variants: The gods say nothing of fear, yet this morning their thrones have moved back from the edge of the Divine Realm. A herd of divine beasts has broken its ancient bonds and is running.

events.text: There are no clouds, and there is a storm. It stands over you alone, a column of dark air with lightning walking in it, and it does not move when you move. Heaven has decided you are too tall.

choices.text: Look up into it

effects.log: Something in the storm looks back. It is not angry. It is measuring.

choices.text: Think about how strong you have become

effects.log: Strong enough for heaven to notice. That was always going to happen.

choices.text: Think about hiding

effects.log: You could make yourself small. You are not sure you want to.

variants: A storm stands over you under a cloudless sky: a pillar of dark air, lightning pacing inside it. When you walk, it walks. Heaven has decided you are too tall.
Out of a clear sky a column of storm comes down and plants itself over your head, and stays. Lightning turns in it like a guard dog. Heaven thinks you have grown too much.

events.text: Immortals around you have started to step back when you pass, not from respect: from the sky. Wherever you stand, the air above you crackles. Heaven pushes back on the strong, and you are, now, the strong.

choices.text: Stand still and let them watch

effects.log: They watch. Some of them are waiting to see you fall. Some of them hope you will not.

choices.text: Ask an old immortal what to do

effects.log: "Hide, or fight, or bow," they say. "Heaven has no fourth door."

choices.text: Walk somewhere alone

effects.log: You walk alone. The storm walks with you.

variants: Wherever you stand, the air above you hums and crackles, and those around you have learned to keep a few steps away. Heaven pushes back on the strong, and you are the strong now.
Others step aside when you pass, and it is not courtesy: the sky over you is crackling. Heaven leans its weight on whoever stands too high, and that is you.

events.text: The lightning comes down a hand's width from your feet and stays there, humming, like a dog that has found what it was sent for. A voice with no throat asks what you think you are.

choices.text: Answer it

effects.log: You tell it exactly what you are. The lightning hums a little louder.

choices.text: Say nothing

effects.log: You say nothing. Silence is an answer too, and heaven writes it down.

choices.text: Laugh

effects.log: You laugh. You do not know where it came from. The storm does not laugh back.

variants: A bolt comes down a hand's breadth from your foot and does not leave. It hums there like a hound that has found its quarry, and a voice without a throat asks what you think you are.
The lightning lands beside you and stays, humming, patient. Then the voice comes, from nowhere and everywhere: what do you think you are?

events.text: A stranger has been asking questions about you at every teahouse on the Isles: what you carry, where you sleep, who stands with you. The tea-sellers tell you because they like you better.

choices.text: Thank the tea-sellers

effects.log: They wave it off. Up here, everyone knows what happens to the strong who sleep soundly.

choices.text: Ask what the stranger looked like

effects.log: Patient, they say. Very patient. The worst kind.

choices.text: Take stock of what you hold

effects.log: You take stock. Every precious thing you own is a reason for someone to come.

events.text: At the top there is no law but strength, and strength wants things. Someone of your own rank wants something of yours. They have not hidden it, which is its own kind of message.

choices.text: Find out what they want

effects.log: You find out. It is the thing you would least like to lose.

choices.text: Find out who they are

effects.log: A cultivator with a long name and longer grudges. Not a fool.

choices.text: Decide it does not frighten you

effects.log: You decide. Your body has not been told.

events.text: A letter arrives with no seal, only a name you do not know and three words: I will come. Whoever wrote it pressed hard enough to tear the paper.

choices.text: Burn the letter

effects.log: It burns. The words stay with you.

choices.text: Keep the letter

effects.log: You keep it. Someday you may want to show it to its writer.

choices.text: Write back

effects.log: You write back two words: I know. It feels good.

events.text: The summons comes on a tablet of white jade, and it is not a request. Beyond the edge of the heavens something presses in, and the courts send their strong to hold the line. Your name is on the list.

choices.text: Read the list of names

effects.log: Some of the names you know. Some of them you will know better soon.

choices.text: Ask what the frontier is like

effects.log: The ones who have been there do not describe it. They only say: go with friends.

choices.text: Put the tablet down and think

effects.log: The tablet glows quietly on your table. It will not go away.

events.text: Rank above the clouds is a duty as well as a crown. A herald stands at your door with the frontier's call, and behind the herald's polite face you can see they are counting how many of the called come back.

choices.text: Ask the herald how many come back

effects.log: Most, the herald says. Then, more honestly: many.

choices.text: Thank the herald

effects.log: The herald bows. It is a hard job, carrying that tablet.

choices.text: Close the door gently

effects.log: You close the door. The call is still in your hand.

events.text: You sit with both your Daos at once, as if holding two rivers in two hands. For a moment they almost meet. Then they spring apart, and you are holding two rivers again.

choices.text: Breathe, and begin again

effects.log: You begin again. That is most of what a fusion is.

choices.text: Ask what you did wrong

effects.log: You did nothing wrong. They are not ready to be one thing. Neither are you.

events.text: The first year of the fusion. You hold your two Daos side by side until their edges blur, and where they touch something new flickers: not either of them, something else.

choices.text: Look closely at the new thing

effects.log: It has no name yet. It looks back at you as if it is waiting to be given one.

choices.text: Hold still and let it grow

effects.log: You hold still. A year of stillness, and the new thing is a little larger.

events.text: The second year. The two Daos run into each other now like rivers at a confluence, churning. Some days you are not sure where you end and the new law begins.

choices.text: Keep your own name in your mouth

effects.log: You say your own name every morning. It helps more than you expected.

choices.text: Let the churning carry you

effects.log: It carries you a long way. When it puts you down, the law is nearer.

events.text: The third year. You open your eyes and the sky is not quite the sky it was: there is a law in it that was not there before, and it answers to you.

choices.text: Name it

effects.log: You give it a name. The sky seems to agree.

choices.text: Thank the two Daos it was made from

effects.log: You thank them. Neither is gone. Both are in it.

events.text: Below the clouds a child is born in a valley of rice terraces, and a small part of you is born with them. The child is slow to talk and quick to watch: the frogs, the water, the old man next door.

choices.text: Let the child watch the water

effects.log: The child learns how water finds its way down a terrace. Far above, you understand something about patience.

choices.text: Let the child follow the old man next door

effects.log: The old man teaches the child to whistle through a blade of grass. They are friends for life.

choices.text: Let the child be a child

effects.log: The child plays in the mud for years. You had forgotten what that was like.

events.text: Your side-self is grown now, with a farmer's hands. A dry year comes, and the upper valley wants to dam the stream that feeds the lower one.

choices.text: Go up and talk to the upper valley

effects.log: It takes a week of talking. In the end the water is shared, and your side-self has made an unlikely friend.

choices.text: Dig a new channel by night

effects.log: The channel works. Nobody ever finds out who dug it. Above, you notice how quietly the clever thing can be done.

choices.text: Break the upper valley's dam

effects.log: The dam breaks, and so does a friendship between valleys. The water comes down anyway.

events.text: Your side-self marries late and well, and raises three children and a great many ducks. Life is the work of the seasons, and the seasons do not wait.

choices.text: Teach the children the terraces

effects.log: The children learn the terraces as their parent did, and the valley goes on.

choices.text: Take in an orphan from the road

effects.log: The orphan grows up in the valley and never leaves it.

choices.text: Work the fields harder than anyone

effects.log: The harvest is the best in the valley for ten years. Your side-self does not notice the children growing up.

events.text: A flood year. The river rises in the night and the lower terraces are going under, and with them the house of the old neighbour's grandchildren.

choices.text: Wade into the flood for them

effects.log: Your side-self goes into the black water with a rope. It is the bravest thing that life ever does.

choices.text: Open the sluice to the empty field

effects.log: The water goes where it is told. Above, you learn something about giving a great force a road.

choices.text: Save your own house first

effects.log: Your own house is saved. The grandchildren are saved by others. Nobody says anything, and everybody knows.

events.text: Old now, your side-self sits on the terrace wall in the evenings and watches the water go down, step by step, the way it always has.

choices.text: Sit with the grandchildren

effects.log: They sit together until the stars come out. Then the life is over, gently, and comes home to you.

choices.text: Watch the water one last time

effects.log: Your side-self watches the water find its way down. Above the clouds, so do you.

choices.text: Close the eyes

effects.log: The eyes close. A whole life folds up small and comes home.

events.text: Your side-self is born to a poor clerk's family in a market town, and learns characters before they can walk properly. There are never enough candles.

choices.text: Read by the light of the shop next door

effects.log: The shopkeeper next door leaves the lamp burning late on purpose. A lifelong friend.

choices.text: Learn the classics by heart

effects.log: The classics go in and stay in. Above, you find old texts clearer than they were.

choices.text: Copy other people's letters for coins

effects.log: The coins buy candles. The letters teach your side-self how people really talk.

events.text: The district exam. Your side-self sits in a cell for three days with a brush and a cold bun, and on the second day a neighbour slides a note under the wall: the answers.

choices.text: Burn the note

effects.log: Your side-self burns the note and writes their own answers. They pass, barely, and honestly.

choices.text: Read it

effects.log: The answers are wrong anyway. Your side-self fails, and learns something about shortcuts.

choices.text: Slide a note back: good luck

effects.log: The neighbour passes too. They will be friends in three provinces.

events.text: A post as a junior clerk in a magistrate's office. The magistrate is lazy and the cases pile up, and the people waiting in the yard have been waiting a long time.

choices.text: Work through the cases by night

effects.log: The yard empties, case by case. Nobody thanks a clerk. Your side-self does not need it.

choices.text: Befriend the people in the yard

effects.log: Your side-self knows every name in the yard by the end of the year.

choices.text: Take a small gift to move a case forward

effects.log: The gift is small. The next one is less small.

events.text: Your side-self finds proof in the records that the magistrate has been selling judgements. Saying so would end a career, perhaps more.

choices.text: Take the proof to the prefect

effects.log: Your side-self walks into the prefect's hall with the records under one arm. It could go either way.

choices.text: Copy the proof and hide it well

effects.log: The copy waits in a wall for years. Above, you learn the long patience of a hidden thing.

choices.text: Burn the proof and keep the post

effects.log: The post is kept. Some nights your side-self does not sleep.

events.text: Grey-haired, your side-self teaches poor children their characters in the back of a temple, by the light of a lamp a neighbour leaves burning late.

choices.text: Teach one more lesson

effects.log: One more lesson, and then the last. The children never forget it, and neither do you.

choices.text: Write down what a life taught

effects.log: A thin book, in a careful hand. It comes home with the soul, and reads differently above.

choices.text: Put the brush down

effects.log: The brush goes down. The life folds closed like a book.

events.text: Your side-self is born on the road, the child of travelling players, and grows up between towns with a wooden sword and a great deal of nerve.

choices.text: Let the child practise with the wooden sword

effects.log: Thousands of swings in the dust. Above, your own hand remembers something it had forgotten.

choices.text: Let the child make friends in every town

effects.log: In every town there is someone who waves when the wagons come in.

choices.text: Let the child pick fights

effects.log: The child wins most of them. The ones they lose teach more.

events.text: Grown, your side-self takes the road alone with a real sword and a little skill. At a mountain pass a band of robbers is stopping travellers.

choices.text: Clear the pass

effects.log: Your side-self clears the pass and sends the robbers off with bruises and a lecture.

choices.text: Join the travellers and get them through

effects.log: The travellers get through, and one of them becomes your side-self's sworn friend.

choices.text: Take the robbers' takings for yourself

effects.log: The takings are heavy. Your side-self tells no one where they came from.

events.text: Your side-self has a name now in three provinces, and a rival who wants it. The rival is very good, and very young.

choices.text: Spar with the rival and teach them

effects.log: The rival loses, and comes back next year better. A friendship made of bruises.

choices.text: Study the rival's style

effects.log: There is something in it your side-self has never seen. Above, you see it too.

choices.text: Humiliate the rival in public

effects.log: The rival is humiliated. Your side-self's name grows, and so does something meaner.

events.text: A walled town is being squeezed by a warlord's men, and the townsfolk have pooled their savings to hire one sword. Yours.

choices.text: Stand at the gate alone

effects.log: Your side-self stands at the town gate with the warlord's men in front of it. This is what the road was for.

choices.text: Teach the townsfolk to defend themselves

effects.log: A month of drills. When the men come, the town is ready. Above, you learn what teaching costs and pays.

choices.text: Take the money and leave in the night

effects.log: The money is taken. The town is left. The road is very quiet that night.

events.text: Your side-self is old and the sword hangs on a wall. Young fighters come to the door sometimes to ask about the old days.

choices.text: Tell them the truth about the old days

effects.log: The truth is less glorious than the stories, and more useful. They listen.

choices.text: Take the sword down one last time

effects.log: One last form, slow, in the courtyard at dawn. Every move of a life is in it.

choices.text: Let the young ones believe the stories

effects.log: Let them have the stories. Your side-self smiles, and the life comes home.

events.text: Your side-self is born in a mountain village to the herb-woman's daughter, and grows up with dirt under their nails and the names of a hundred plants in their mouth.

choices.text: Learn every plant on the mountain

effects.log: Every plant, every season. Above, you find you understand how living things mend.

choices.text: Follow the herb-woman on her rounds

effects.log: Every house in the village knows the child by name. Some of them owe the child their lives later.

choices.text: Run wild on the mountain

effects.log: The child knows every cliff and cave. That will matter one day.

events.text: A fever comes through the valley, and the village headman wants the sick carried up to the old shrine and left there, so the fever will not spread.

choices.text: Nurse them in the shrine yourself

effects.log: Your side-self nurses them for a month. Most live.

choices.text: Find what the fever is

effects.log: It is in the well. Your side-self finds it. Above, you see the hidden cause of a thing more easily.

choices.text: Do as the headman says

effects.log: The sick are carried up and left. Some of them come down again. Some do not.

events.text: A wealthy merchant's son falls from his horse on the mountain road, and the merchant offers your side-self a fortune to come to the city as the family physician.

choices.text: Go to the city

effects.log: The city teaches your side-self a great deal about medicine and more about people.

choices.text: Stay with the village

effects.log: The fortune goes to someone else. The village keeps its healer.

choices.text: Go, and charge the village too when you come back

effects.log: Your side-self comes back rich and stays rich. The village pays.

events.text: A plague village two valleys over. Nobody will go in. The soldiers at the road say anyone who goes in does not come out until it is over, one way or the other.

choices.text: Go in

effects.log: Your side-self goes past the soldiers with a basket of herbs and does not look back.

choices.text: Send medicines over the wall

effects.log: Every day a basket over the wall. It is not enough, and it is not nothing. Above, you learn the measure of what one can give.

choices.text: Turn back

effects.log: Your side-self turns back. The village two valleys over is not spoken of again.

events.text: Old, your side-self still walks the rounds, slower now, with an apprentice carrying the basket who knows the names of a hundred plants.

choices.text: Hand the basket over for good

effects.log: The apprentice takes the basket. The village has its healer. The life comes home content.

choices.text: Walk the mountain one more time

effects.log: Every plant, in its season, one last time. You remember them all, above.

choices.text: Sit by the fire

effects.log: The fire burns down. So, gently, does the life.

events.text: Your side-self is born on a river barge and learns to swim before they can walk. The river is road, market and home.

choices.text: Learn the river's moods

effects.log: Every eddy and sandbar. Above, you understand how a great force can be read.

choices.text: Make friends on every barge

effects.log: There is no barge on that river where your side-self is a stranger.

choices.text: Learn to haggle

effects.log: The child can haggle a fishwife into a bad mood by nine. A useful gift.

events.text: Grown, your side-self runs their own ferry. A smuggler offers good silver to carry certain boxes across, no questions asked.

choices.text: Refuse the smuggler

effects.log: The smuggler shrugs and finds another ferry. Your side-self sleeps well.

choices.text: Carry the boxes

effects.log: The silver is good. The boxes are heavy. Your side-self does not ask.

choices.text: Warn the other ferrymen about the smuggler

effects.log: The ferrymen take note. The river is a family.

events.text: Trade is good. Your side-self has three ferries now and a warehouse, and a rival merchant who wants the crossing for himself.

choices.text: Offer the rival a partnership

effects.log: The rival is surprised into agreeing. Partners, and in the end, friends.

choices.text: Undercut him until he gives up

effects.log: He gives up. The crossing is yours. Above, you see how a long game is won.

choices.text: Have his warehouse burned

effects.log: It burns. Nobody can prove anything. Your side-self never crosses that part of the river at night again.

events.text: The great flood. The river is three times its width and the village on the far bank is going under, and every ferryman on the river says no boat can cross.

choices.text: Cross anyway

effects.log: Your side-self takes the strongest ferry out into the flood. Nobody on the bank breathes.

choices.text: Rope the ferries together into a bridge

effects.log: It holds for one night, long enough. Above, you learn how many small things make one great one.

choices.text: Moor the ferries and wait

effects.log: The ferries are safe. The village on the far bank is not.

events.text: Old, your side-self sits on the warehouse steps and watches someone else's children run the ferries back and forth across the river, the way it always was.

choices.text: Wave to every ferry that passes

effects.log: Every ferry waves back. The whole river knows you.

choices.text: Watch the river one last time

effects.log: The river goes on. So, above, do you, a little wiser.

choices.text: Close the ledger

effects.log: The last line in the ledger. The life comes home.

events.text: The first temple to you is a small one, built by people who could not afford it. Across the villages they burn incense to you now, and ask you for rain, for sons, for the fever to pass. You are still only what you were. They do not seem to mind.

choices.text: Visit the first temple

effects.log: You stand at the back while they pray to you. Nobody recognises you. It is the strangest hour of your life.

choices.text: Listen to what they ask for

effects.log: Mostly small things. You find you want to give them all of them.

choices.text: Leave the temple to its keepers

effects.log: The keepers sweep it every morning. It does not need you to be holy.

events.text: Nobody across the villages says your name aloud now; they say the title instead, and lower their voices for it. Tribute arrives at your gate on the first of every month, carried by people who do not look up.

choices.text: Take the tribute without a word

effects.log: You take it. Fear is a kind of worship too, and it pays on time.

choices.text: Look at the faces of those who carry it

effects.log: They are afraid of you. Something in you is glad, and something older is not.

choices.text: Send one of them home with their tribute

effects.log: The story of it goes further than any cruelty would have. It frightens them more.
